key_insight: A fault-tolerant quantum algorithm is proposed to compute open-system battery cathode observables by embedding strongly coupled electron-lattice and reservoir dynamics into a unitary, chain-mapped Caldeira-Leggett simulation.
engineering_relevance: The method targets practical prediction of open-circuit voltage and differential capacity for battery cathodes, with resource estimates that indicate feasibility only at large fault-tolerant scale.
method: Chain-map the baths to make open-system dynamics unitary and Trotterizable
Use a 4th-order Trotter step with polynomial T-gate scaling
Calibrate/validate against HEOM at strong coupling and Lindblad behavior at weak coupling
evidence_signal: The abstract reports agreement with benchmark models and battery experiments, including a LiFePO4 voltage peak within ±5 mV and a LiMn2O4 two-plateau split of 125 mV versus an observed 150 mV.
watch_item: The proposed full voltage-curve simulation remains extremely resource-intensive, requiring about 368 logical qubits and ~1.7×10^12 T-gates, so it is not yet practical on near-term hardware.
paper_title: Quantum Algorithm for Open-System Battery Cathodes by Modeling Multiple Strongly Coupled Holstein Polarons with Chain-Mapped Caldeira-Leggett Dynamics
